newsitem.title: UK: Stocks end lower in London, Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Stocks end lower in London, Tokyo.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - The threat of higher U.S. interest rates sent British shares lower for the second day running amid concern that interest rates might be raised in Britain as early as next month. The FTSE 100 leading share index closed, which dropped nearly 50 points on Monday, ended 37.7 points down at 4,607.5.

FRANKFURT - German shares closed bourse trade lower as traders remained cautious ahead of the meeting of the Federal Reserve, with the main market feature being drug group BASF's lawsuit woes. The DAX-30 blue-chip index closed trade 61.12 points lower at 3,543.43. In post-bourse trade the index fell 53.06 to 3,516.20.

PARIS - French shares finished more than 1 percent lower as investors took profits on last week's rise of more than 5 percent. Traders said weakness in bonds and the dollar ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting also encouraged sellers. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 33.17 points at 2,751.11.

ZURICH - After a string of record closes last week, shares ended more than 1 percent lower, dragged down by losses in index-heavyweight shares. Dealers said Wall Street's early weakness and the fall in the dollar put blue-chip stocks such as Novartis, Roche and Nestle under pressure. The blue-chip SMI slid 76.5 points, or 1.48 percent, to 5,081.0 and the all-share SPI was down 41.63 points to 3,214.28 points.

TOKYO - Stocks slipped, weighed down by damage to exporter issues from the yen's strength against the dollar, brokers said. News that prosecutors had raided Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd. in a widening investigation into links between financial firms and racketeers also hurt sentiment, they said. The Nikkei average fell 156.92 points to close at 20,332.83.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index surged to new record highs as increased buying on HSBC Holdings and property stocks in the afternoon carried the index to its third record close in eight sessions. The Hang Seng ended up 127.38 points at a closing record of 14,236.20, after hitting an all-time intra-day high of 14,253.97 in late trade.

SYDNEY - Australian stocks ended barely changed with all eyes on the United States as traders waited to assess any rate implications of the Federal Reserve meeting. The All Ordinaries Index shed a wafer-thin 0.3 points to 2,530.7.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended down as fears of a U.S. interest rate rise swept global markets and knocked industrial shares firmly into negative territory. The all-share index dropped 10.4 points to 7,106.2, the industrial index dipped 26.5 points to 8,372.0. The golds index climbed 20.3 points to 1,213.1.
